source_reads.actual_read_scope: Original Overview, Symptoms, When to see a doctor, Causes, Risk factors, Complications, Prevention and reference list read; web lines269–354,366–372. Adult/general aortic dissection education. Same Mayo authorship group as treatment and beta-blocker pages; references include UpToDate, AskMayoExpert2023 and Ferri2025.

Original page read: Overview55–71; Symptoms/Causes75–128; Diagnosis133–144; Treatment149–161; Outlook175–178; Prevention182–191; Living With195–219; References246–255. Adult/general education. References AHA, StatPearls, Merck and observational studies; separate institutional writing, not independent trials.

Original Diagnosis269–282 and Treatment286–298, reference list316–321 read. Adult acute A/B dissection and follow-up. Same Mayo editorial group; shares UpToDate/AskMayoExpert/Ferri upstream with symptom page.

Original PDF text read cover, pp1–6 and10: objectives; pain may have disappeared p3; risk assessment; anti-impulse therapy p4; CTA p5; urgent A/complicated B care p10. Review due2027-03-01. Regional adult hospital/transfer protocol, not a patient dosing recipe. Flowchart-layout screenshot retrieval was not usable; no branching score/transfer category or dosing algorithm reproduced.

Original official summary read, points2–5: imaging reports, teams, shared decisions, family history, genetic testing and first-degree-relative imaging. Same joint guideline upstream as part2; not counted independently of it.

Original page read sections About15–28, Side effects54–68, suitability/pregnancy77–85, interactions88–98. Displayed last review2026-09-04. Medicine-class information, not aortic-specific efficacy; independently authored national NHS material.

Original Aortic Aneurysm—Living With page read, web94–113: surveillance, complications, medicines and lifting precautions. Applied only to shared aortic mechanisms and recovery precautions; not used as dissection-specific operative guidance. NIH subdivisions share one editorial group.

Original ACC official Key Perspectives Part2 summary read, paragraphs6–8, web161–202. Especially AAS acute management, surveillance and pregnancy. Summary only; full guideline was not attested read. Joint2022 ACC/AHA guideline; part1, part2 and guideline physical-activity extract are one editorial group.

Original How they work264–265, Side effects292–310 read: fatigue/cold extremities/dizziness and abrupt cessation warning. Same Mayo group as disease pages; no independent-pair credit between Mayo pages.

Original Pharmacy leaflet actually read: What else should I know about this medicine? (web283), explicit do not stop suddenly; source version2/ST0568, updated2024-01-09. Locally authored pharmacy material, distinct from national NHS medicines page; no independent-trial claim.

Original2025 guideline HTML sections8.1–8.4 and8.6 actually read (web2818–2868) and pre-pregnancy overview3978: risk after root repair, pregnancy/postpartum monitoring, aortic/Pregnancy Heart Team, pre-pregnancy whole-aorta imaging. No claim of reading every guideline section. Exact publication day not extracted. Independent ESC writing with overlapping studies/guidelines, not independent trial replication.

Official JACC indexed section7.3.1 Initial Medical Management of AAS, Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text item3 actually read: beta-blocker cautions include acute aortic regurgitation, heart block and bradycardia; alternatives are clinician decisions. Retrieval limited to this official indexed passage; direct full article not attested. Same2022 ACC/AHA guideline and group as summaries/slide set, not independent of them.

Original Heart-Healthy Living—Choose Heart-Healthy Foods read: DASH99–100, food groups103–119, sodium124–135. General cardiovascular nutrition, not a dissection repair treatment or a universal renal diet. NIH subdivisions are one group.

Original Why healthy eating129–134, Liquids144–146, Protein153–157, individualized plan164–170, Track liquids185–187 and review date276 read. Last reviewed2025-01, exact day absent. Only people with coexisting chronic kidney disease; not extrapolated to all acute kidney injuries. Same NIH group as NHLBI.

Original recovery/activity108–155 and Eating and drinking156–167 read. Resource5456/VER1, published2023-12, review2026-12; exact day not displayed. Applied only after open cardiac surgery for appetite, balanced food and existing special diets. Locally authored hospital material; national NHS medicine page is not treated as a separate trial. No sternotomy lifting-weight limits extrapolated to all dissections.

Official AHA-hosted guideline slide set actually read PDF pp214–215 (zero-based213–214), printed slides214–215: Physical Activity and Quality of Life recommendations1–4, lines2567–2592. Corroborating official JACC indexed supportive prose also read; direct JACC full article403 and PMC recaptcha are not full-read attestations. Same2022 ACC/AHA guideline group as summaries; no numerical exercise prescription imported.

changes: Retained14 detailed bilingual sections and original acute A/B, repair and complication content.
Distinguished emergency acute suspicion even after pain settles from stable chronic follow-up.
Added beta-blocker tolerability and explicit pregnancy/postpartum coordination with ESC2025; retained genetic/family follow-up.
Bound ordinary recordkeeping as explanation; all critical action/risk/benefit claims retain independent writing support.
Narrowed renal nutrition to actually supported coexisting CKD and added concrete open-cardiac-surgery eating support; no blanket fluid restriction.

suggested_p0_leaf_scope.include_concept: Aortic dissection acute recognition and chronic follow-up; thoracic, abdominal or combined location and with/without mention of rupture need mapping owner semantic review.
suggested_p0_leaf_scope.classification_boundary: BD50.0Z/BD50.1Z mean without mention of perforation or rupture, not proof of no rupture. No coding entries changed; not all aneurysm/penetrating-ulcer/intramural-haematoma leaves are established by this article.
suggested_p0_leaf_scope.special_cases: Generic emergency description does not establish complete treatment for every obstetric, traumatic, inherited syndrome or rupture subtype.
